sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Excess Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors and Resistors

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty between the Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) and the People's Republic of China for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 1984, in force 1986)
Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (signed 1994, in force 1995)
Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 2010, in force 2011)
Treaty between the Benelux States and other counterparties on establishment and legal persons (Benelux Convention of 1960)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between the EU and Canada (provisionally applied 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated and amended (notably by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 17 July 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended, and CSSF Circulars 19/732, 20/744 and 22/811; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010 on organizational measures; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds. Competent authorities: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each shareholder's and each UBO's passport (passeport) with notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority of each individual's residence jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Luxembourg is party to the HCCH Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961, ratified 1979) or consular legalization for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from criminal record (extrait du casier judiciaire) of each director, manager, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority of each person's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and register of directors / shareholders of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; original-issued within the last three months

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (attestation de référence bancaire) for each corporate shareholder or sponsor confirming source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification of signature, then Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the bank is outside the EU

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation (procuration aux fins de constitution) authorizing the local resident incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent public authority of the principal's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; if drafted outside Luxembourg, the signature must be authenticated before the local Luxembourg consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, statutory managers, shareholders above 25%, and UBOs against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists under Council Regulations (EU) No. 269/2014 and No. 833/2014, as amended; (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list; (iii) the OFAC SDN list for all USD-denominated correspondent banking and Swift wire transactions; (iv) the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance national restrictive measures list; and (v) commercial PEP databases (World-Check / Factiva) with enhanced due diligence triggered by any politically exposed person designation, in accordance with CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Law of 12 November 2004. Adverse hits must be immediately escalated to the CRF and the intended bank's compliance department; no structuring advice may circumvent EU or UN sanctions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic filing portal at https://www.lbr.lu or https://brc.lbr.lu; physical desk: RCS, 15-17 Boulevard Roosevelt, L-2450 Luxembourg.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names of an SARL must be registered in Latin script and must include the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL'. Accepted working languages are French, German, and Luxembourgish. Names originating in non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew) must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet by a sworn translator; the transliterated string becomes the sole registered name and a French translation of its meaning must be appended to the articles of association. The name must be factually distinctive and non-misleading under Article 159-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Assurance / Réassurance (requires Commissariat aux Assurances - CAA license)
Fonds / FCP / FOP / SICAV / SICAR / RAIF (requires CSSF authorization or registration)
État / National / Luxembourg (misleading affiliation with the State or public authorities)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross (protected emblem under Geneva Conventions)
P.S.F. / PFS (Professionnel du Secteur Financier - requires CSSF license)
Fiduciaire / Trust / Trustee (requires CSSF license or regulated trust company status)
EU / European Union / NATO / UN / Benelux (intergovernmental and institutional names)
Scandalous, offensive, or grossly misleading denominations irrespective of language
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the RCS, the applicant shall: (1) file a corrected name proposal through the LBR portal without losing file precedence; (2) submit a formal written objection to the RCS registrar attaching trademark registration certificates or documented prior use; (3) if unresolved, file a petition for review with the Minister of Justice under the Law of 15 June 2004 on administrative procedure; and (4) appeal the final refusal to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) of Luxembourg within three months of notification. Urgent interim suspension of the refusal may be requested from the President of the Administrative Tribunal. The registrar's refusal is based on factual distinctiveness and public-order sensitivity; trademark ownership disputes are resolved by the civil courts and do not bind the registrar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) approved under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended. A pure virtual mailbox without physical infrastructure or personnel is discouraged and is not bankable. For an ISIC 4652 wholesale distributor of passive electronic components, Luxembourg banks and the tax administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA - AED) generally accept a domiciled registered office provided the company demonstrates real commercial substance: at least one resident director or statutory manager, substantive board decisions taken in Luxembourg, a Luxembourg VAT registration (RCVA), and operational contracts with third-party logistics providers managing inventory. Substantive presence at the registered office must be verifiable under Circular LIR 162/6 on substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk - approximately 25% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the AED, RCS officials, or the bank's KYC team within the first 24 months following incorporation. The likelihood increases to approximately 60% if the company claims VAT refunds, applies for customs authorizations, or maintains the registered office at a domiciliation address in a building housing more than 50 legal entities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of French-language articles of association (statuts) for a standard SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg avocat (law firm admitted to the Barreau de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market flat fee for a standard single-shareholder SARL; benchmark hourly rate of USD 280-390 per hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) before a Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaire luxembourgeois (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff schedule (tarif notarial) scaled by share capital; standard fee band for EUR 12,394.68 minimum capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the company with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via electronic filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS fee schedule; EUR 19.98 for electronic filing plus incidental administrative costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed in the RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff per the official gazette fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Compulsory affiliation and first-year levy with the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chambre de Commerce du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory annual cotisation imposed on merchants and companies; pro-rated for the first fiscal year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Share capital deposit into the notary's blocked account (statutory minimum capital)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary's escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BIL, BCEE, Société Générale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum SARL capital of EUR 12,394.68 under Article 152 of the Law of 10 August 1915; USD equivalent at prevailing EUR/USD exchange rate; amount is not a fee and is subsequently released to the company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service, first full year, licensed domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation company (agréée by the Ministry of Justice under the Law of 12 November 2004)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for quality level-2 domiciliation in Luxembourg City including mail handling, meeting room access, and registrar correspondence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial beneficial owner (UBO) declaration filing with the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free of charge; if delegated to the registered agent, customary service fee of USD 80-120 may apply

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille bundle for UBO and shareholder identification documents, and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authorities of each document's country of origin (notaries, ministries of foreign affairs, consulates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille tariffs vary by issuing state; consular legalization fees apply for non-Hague states; estimated USD 100-400 per bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traduction assermentée) of apostilled documents into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered with the Luxembourg district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-annexed expert tariff per page; typical 12-15 page bundle at USD 25-35 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LuxTrust authentication token for LBR/RCS, e-filing, and future RBE declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published LuxTrust tariff for the token with two-year validity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation bank AML/KYC onboarding package and adverse-media reporting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service tariff for AML/CFT due diligence file preparation under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as consolidated; SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 through 710-25, in particular Article 710-4 (minimum capital), Article 710-15 (manager appointment), and Article 710-24 (registered office).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the single digital portal myguichet.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif et statuts — notarially executed deed of incorporation and articles of association, filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000 under Article 710-4; full subscription and full payment in cash required at incorporation; each share has a minimum nominal value of EUR 1; capital must be deposited into a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution and released only upon RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The founder/shareholder approves the incorporation of [●] SARL with a fully subscribed and paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000 pursuant to Articles 710-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies. RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office is established at [●] in the City of Luxembourg and the managers shall execute all notarial and RCS filings. RESOLVED FURTHER: Mr./Ms. [●] is appointed sole manager (gérant) with powers of full management, including bank account opening, contracting, hiring and tax filings. RESOLVED FURTHER: The manager's statement of subscription and payment of capital is approved and filed. RESOLVED FINALLY: All prior preparatory acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Single Luxembourg notary (Notaire) acting under the Chamber of Notaries (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles in French or German, arrange signing date before the notary, and ensure the instrument is executed by the founder. Simultaneously execute the manager's statement of subscription and payment of capital (déclaration de souscription et libération). If a name reservation was obtained, annex the RCS name certificate. The notary authenticates the deed and is responsible for onward transmission of all required documents to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (dated, in French or German)
Passport or national ID of founding shareholder(s) and manager(s)
Name reservation certificate (obtained via myguichet.lu)
Payment details of share capital and confirmation of blocked account
Power of attorney if a corporate founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a deficiency, correct the factual inconsistencies in the draft statutes, re-execute a corrected deed before the same notary, and pay only revised notary fees; no additional state filing fee is triggered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., Luxembourg branch of a licensed bank) operating under CSSF supervision.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the company name, deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital, and obtain a bank confirmation letter (attestation de blocage) evidencing the deposit. The account remains frozen until the RCS registration certificate is issued. The bank issues a capital release letter following registration.
required_dossiers: Notarially executed or draft deed of incorporation
Identity documents of the account signatories
Beneficial owner declaration and extract from the RCS once available
Bank account opening forms and compliance/AML questionnaire
Blocked account deposit instruction letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen bank refuses the account, approach an alternative Luxembourg credit institution and provide the notary's certificate of capital payment or the blocked account confirmation; the deficiency is cured by obtaining a substitute attestation de blocage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), submitted online via myguichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed and all statutory annexes through the notary's LBR filing. Pay the online registration fee. The RCS verifies legal compliance, issues the registration certificate (extrait), and assigns the RCS legal identifier (Matricule) and LEI reference. The company acquires legal personality upon entry in the register.
required_dossiers: Notarially executed deed of incorporation
Articles of association
Manager's declaration of subscription and payment of capital
Bank attestation of blocked capital deposit
Identity extract and criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of the manager
Beneficial owner register declaration (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any RCS deficiency notice within one month by submitting corrected or translated documents through the LBR online portal; if a legalization or apostille is missing, supply the notarized copy and re-submit before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés (RES) — official electronic publication service of the Luxembourg Official Journal operated by the Ministry of Justice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or company files the required excerpt of the deed and the manager appointment information with the RES. The RES publishes the constitutive data (company name, form, capital, registered office, managers, legal representative). Publication is a statutory condition for the effectiveness of the deed against third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait)
Deed excerpt and articles summary submitted via myguichet.lu
Manager appointment attachment
Identity of beneficial owner where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication data is erroneous, file an errata request through the RES web service within 15 days and provide the corrected RCS extract; the published text is then replaced by the corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, Social Security and Statistical Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Administration de l'Enregistrement (AEDT), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), and STATEC via myguichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the business registration form to obtain the Luxembourg corporate tax number (NIF), register for VAT after submission of the VAT Form 1, register the employer at CCSS for social contributions, and obtain the STATEC statistical enterprise number. Apply for an EORI number if the company will import or export goods. Complete the registration within 15 days of RCS enrolment.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Articles of association
Identity of the manager and director
Bank account confirmation
Proof of registered office (lease agreement)
Form 1 for VAT and employer registration questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT or tax number is delayed, file a follow-up via the ACD/VAT desk at myguichet.lu; a late registration may be cured by submitting a complement to the initial declaration and by settling any nominal late-filing penalty through the AEDT.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction générale de l'industrie (Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy, Industry Directorate) for reference in case of future expansion; no industrial license required for wholesale distribution of passive electronic inventory under ISIC 4652.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — the activity qualifies as pure wholesale distribution. A standard RCS business registration covers the commercial activity; a Class 4 declaration under the Law of 9 May 2022 on classified establishments (établissements classés) applies only if warehousing floor area exceeds 1,000 m².

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement — Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA; the distribution activity falls outside Annexes I and II of the Law of 9 May 2022. A simple written declaration (déclaration) is required only where dedicated warehousing area exceeds 1,000 m² or where batteries/chemical substances are stored, otherwise no classified-establishment filing is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge, VOC emission or hazardous waste generated in normal handling of multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors; compliance, if applicable, with EU Regulation 2016/1628 on emissions of non-road mobile machinery for warehouse equipment, Directive 2000/53/EC on end-of-life vehicles for transport equipment, and the WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU for disposal of defective electronic inventory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: obtain a fire safety certificate from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for any occupied warehouse premises. Structural clearance: verify that the leased building complies with the municipal building permit (autorisation de construire) and the confirmed structural load inspection. Occupational clearance: register the workplace with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under Article L.610-1 of the Luxembourg Labor Code, notify all working staff before first work, and display the internal safety regulations; if staffing exceeds 25 employees, establish a joint works council representation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) for corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (EIS) and net wealth tax (IF); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT - Registration, Estates and VAT Administration) for value added tax (TVA); Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration) for export controls. Digital service portals: MyGuichet.lu, Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCSe), eCDF/eTax for direct tax filings, and the AEDT electronic VAT filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent establishing a Luxembourg SARL must: (1) execute notarized articles of association before a Luxembourg notary and file them with the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) through Luxembourg Business Registers; (2) obtain the national identification number (numéro d'identification / matricule, 15-digit format) issued ex officio by the CTIE, which serves as the central business master file identifier; (3) submit VAT registration form 640 to the AEDT to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits) before carrying out any taxable supply; a foreign-owned SARL is registrable from the first euro, with no de minimis threshold; (4) register for IRC, EIS and IF with the ACD, which opens a corporate tax file (numéro d'affiliation); (5) appoint a Luxembourg-resident manager (gérant) and, where statutory thresholds are exceeded (balance sheet over EUR 4.4 million; net turnover over EUR 8.8 million; over 25 employees), an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé). No sectoral license is required for wholesale distribution of electronic components (ISIC 4652). All registrations are completed electronically via MyGuichet.lu, with the registered office (siège social) as the sole physical presence requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Luxembourg-resident SARL is fully taxable at entity level and is not a pass-through vehicle. It is subject to corporate income tax (IRC) at 17% headline rate, a 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC, municipal business tax (EIS) at rates between 6.75% and 10.5% depending on the commune (10.5% in Luxembourg City), producing an approximate combined effective corporate rate of 24.94% in Luxembourg City; net wealth tax (IF) of 0.5% applies to taxable net assets exceeding EUR 500,000, with a minimum net wealth tax. Worldwide income is taxable, subject to territorial carve-outs for qualifying foreign permanent establishments and the participation exemption (article 166 LIR) for qualifying shareholdings (at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost, held for 12 months). Non-resident ownership of 100% of the SARL is permitted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not have a US-style check-the-box regime; available elections include: (i) participation exemption election (article 166 LIR) on a per-shareholding basis; (ii) IP box election (article 50bis LIR) granting an 80% exemption on net qualifying IP income; (iii) group taxation (fiscal unity) election under articles 164bis-164ter LIR permitting 99% profit and loss transfer among Luxembourg-resident companies with a 75% or greater holding; (iv) VAT grouping election under article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law treating the SARL and its 90%-controlled Luxembourg affiliates as a single taxable person; (v) hybrid mismatch substantiation elections under ATAD implementation (articles 168ter-168septies LIR) for reverse hybrid structures; and (vi) Pillar Two top-up tax election for in-scope MNE groups under the law of 22 December 2023. For a passive electronic inventory trading SARL, the recommended elections are VAT grouping and participation exemption on any equity stakes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 as amended and EU Directive 2006/112/EC, administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-resident suppliers: any taxable supply made in Luxembourg triggers mandatory VAT registration from the first euro. Luxembourg-established small enterprises may elect the franchise exemption under article 57 of the VAT Law for annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000, but a foreign-owned trading SARL will not qualify in practice. Intra-EU distance sales of the electronic components are governed by the harmonized EUR 10,000 annual distance-selling threshold (OSS scheme), above which Luxembourg VAT is due in the destination Member State. No domestic reverse-charge exception applies to wholesale distribution of electronics; the SARL must charge Luxembourg VAT at 17% on local B2B and B2C sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or tax-authority API validation system. Mandatory structured e-invoicing requirements are: (i) since 1 January 2021, all B2G invoices to Luxembourg public-sector entities must be transmitted via the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 network; (ii) pursuant to the Law of 18 July 2023, with effect from 1 January 2025, every Luxembourg-established taxable person must issue and receive structured electronic invoices in Factur-X / EN 16931-compatible format for B2B transactions, and must retain invoices for 10 years (article 88 of the VAT Law). Exchange is performed through certified PEPPOL access points; there is no government clearance gateway. Taxpayers must maintain a VAT purchase/sales journal and file recapitulative statements (Intrastat / DEB) for intra-EU movements of goods.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies under article 155 of the Luxembourg VAT Law to: (i) exports of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier, the customer, or a third party acting on behalf of either, provided proof of exit from EU territory is obtained within 90 days of the supply; (ii) intra-EU B2B supplies of goods transported to another Member State where the customer communicates a valid EU VAT identification number and both parties file recapitulative statements; and (iii) ancillary services directly linked to the export (freight, inspection, testing, handling). For the passive MLCC and resistor inventory model, the SARL must demonstrate physical removal of warehoused goods from Luxembourg or EU territory through warehouse release documentation, transport evidence, and customs declarations. Consignment and call-off stock movements may benefit from the optional simplification under article 17a of EU Implementing Regulation 282/2011, provided the supplier maintains a consignment stock register; failure to substantiate zero-rating results in recharacterization of the supply as taxable in Luxembourg at 17%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Single Administrative Document / SAD-DAU) or electronic export declaration accepted by Luxembourg Customs within the EU Export Control System (ECS)
Transport document evidencing EU exit: Bill of Lading (sea), CMR/CIM consignment note (road/rail), air waybill (air), or courier receipt with date of departure from EU territory
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying HS codes, Incoterms, quantities, batch references, and VAT registration numbers of both parties
Proof of payment and FX repatriation: Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement evidencing receipt of payment within the contractual term
Warehouse inventory release documentation (picking list, delivery note, stock movement report) evidencing removal from the passive electronic inventory
Customer's valid EU VAT ID validation printout (VIES) and Intrastat DEB declaration for intra-EU supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs apply the 'no proof, no zero-rating' doctrine: where export substantiation is not produced within 90 days from the supply, VAT is reassessed at 17% with late-payment interest of 10% per annum and a 10% late-filing surcharge. In cases of fraud or deliberate falsification under articles 66-68 of the VAT Law, criminal fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years, together with a civil penalty (droits en sus) of up to 100% of the VAT evaded. The reassessment limitation period is 5 years in good faith, extended to 10 years in fraud. Luxembourg Customs conducts post-clearance audits cross-linking export declarations, Intrastat listings, warehouse movement records, and payment flows; refund claims for input VAT on export costs are closely scrutinized, with joint and several liability extending to the SARL managers and the foreign parent company.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating as the national central bank within the Eurosystem and exercising monetary policy, foreign-exchange statistics, and payment-system oversight functions jointly with the European Central Bank (ECB). Prudential supervision of credit institutions and financial intermediaries is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which also issues licensing and AML/CFT regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), guaranteeing free movement of capital and payments. Luxembourg maintains no foreign-exchange control regime and imposes no prior central-bank authorization for current account transactions, capital account movements, or profit remittances. Dividend distributions by a Luxembourg SARL are subject to a 15% withholding tax, reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying shareholdings or to 5%–10% under applicable tax treaties; no exchange-control hurdle applies to the underlying transfer. The composite corporate income tax burden in Luxembourg City is approximately 24.94% (CIT 17% plus solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax). Foreign-currency accounts are freely permitted within and outside Luxembourg, and no BCL approval is required for repatriation or reinvestment of earnings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation-timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Luxembourg. As the euro is a fully convertible reserve currency, the BCL does not require exporters to convert foreign-currency receipts into EUR and does not impose any holding-period restriction; USD, CNY, or other currency balances may be retained indefinitely. The only compliance obligations are (i) balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL under ECB Regulation (EU) 2021/379 and BCL implementing instructions for external transactions above the applicable de minimis thresholds (EUR 12,500 or EUR 50,000 depending on the reporting tail), and (ii) anti-money-laundering reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit for cash or cash-like payments exceeding EUR 10,000 under the amended Law of 28 November 2018, as modified by the Law of 26 March 2023. No surrender certificate or BCL clearing approval is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Formation capital escrow account (compte bloqué) for notarised incorporation; thereafter EUR/USD multi-currency operational account with trade-finance and treasury desks

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital blocking certificate account for SARL share capital; operational current account and deposit-taking treasury lines
Operational account with import letter-of-credit, receivable financing, and supply-chain facilities; capital escrow available at formation
Corporate operational account, SWIFT wire clearing, and documentary collection services
Wholesale corporate account (EUR/USD) for commercial clients; limited retail-style onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. An EU-passported electronic money institution (EMI) licensed by the CSSF or by another EEA regulator under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) may legally open a commercial account for a Luxembourg SARL without a local branch. For the target business (passive electronic-component distribution), an EMI is operationally acceptable as an ancillary sub-account for vendor payments and low-value receivable collection. It is not viable as a primary treasury rail because (i) most EMIs lack documentary letter-of-credit issuance, supply-chain finance, and committed credit-line capabilities; (ii) established tier-1 Luxembourg banks generally decline to aggregate funds flowing only from an offshore EMI owing to end-to-end traceability concerns; and (iii) high-frequency settlement of excess inventory trades requires robust SWIFT, TARGET2, and correspondent-banking corridors that EMIs often route through partner banks with degraded service windows. A CSSF-licensed Luxembourg EMI can be used as a complement, but the anchor banking relationship should remain a supervised commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance or a live video-identification interview with the bank's AML/KYC compliance officer is mandated at the initial underwriting, account-documentation, and activation stage. Remote onboarding is legally possible under Article 4-1 of the amended AML Law of 28 November 2018 (as modified by the Law of 26 March 2023) and CSSF Regulation 12-02, provided the bank deploys an eIDAS-qualified electronic identification method with liveness detection and secure document verification. In market practice, most BCL-licensed tier-1 banks require the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one authorised director to attend an in-person or high-assurance videoconference due-diligence meeting before the banking mandate is countersigned; fully paperless remote opening for a cross-border SARL with non-resident directors is generally rejected or substantially deferred.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership chain terminating in a non-resident holding structure with opaque shareholders or registered agents in non-cooperative jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Luxembourg articles of association, current extract from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (extrait du RCS), declaration of beneficial ownership filed with the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), certified passport copies and address proofs of all directors, a complete shareholding chain diagram signed by the AML responsible person, audited or management financial statements of the ultimate parent, and a Luxembourg substance memorandum evidencing registered office, local governance, accounting support, and economic activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital injection or subsequent shareholder loans, particularly funds routed from third-country related parties or higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation showing remitter, beneficiary, and purpose code; twelve-month bank statements of the transferring entity; signed share-subscription agreement or shareholder loan deed; net-worth evidence supported by audited accounts or certified asset schedules; a signed source-of-wealth statement; and completed CRS/FATCA self-certifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow mismatch: high invoice frequency for passive electronic components without verifiable physical inventory movement, warehousing, or logistics documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supplier and customer framework contracts, purchase orders and order acknowledgements, transport evidence (bill of lading, air waybill, CMR), third-party warehouse receipts, customs import and export declarations, cargo insurance certificates naming the bank as loss-payee where applicable, and a per-SKU stock ledger for MLCC and resistor batches reconciling purchase, storage, and sale quantities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed person (PEP) status of the principal, or sanctions-related hits on trading counterparties located in high-risk third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent name-screening results from World-Check, Dow Jones, or equivalent databases; EU, OFAC, UN, and UK sanctions checklist signed by the compliance officer; counterparty declaration of ultimate ownership and business purpose; underlying trade contracts for all flagged transactions; an external legal opinion from Luxembourg or international counsel; and a residual-risk mitigation memorandum submitted to the bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial share capital and subsequent capital increases must be wired via SWIFT MT103 (for standard commercial amounts) or MT202 COV (for interbank cover transfers) to the SARL's EUR account at the Luxembourg bank. The wire must carry the ECB balance-of-payments purpose code corresponding to the BPM6 category, transactions affecting the reporting enterprise in the form of additions to equity capital, or, for shareholder debt, the intercompany lending code. The beneficiary bank requires the notarised subscription deed, shareholder resolution, proof of the remitter's debit instruction, and final-blocking certificate prior to disbursement. Cash contributions above EUR 50,000 must be consistent with the RBE update and the bank's automatic reporting to the Luxembourg FIU and BCL statistics. No exchange-control approval applies because inbound equity and loan inflows are unrestricted capital movements within the EU/EEA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier, logistics, and commission payments settle via SWIFT MT103 referencing the underlying invoice, or, for euro-denominated EEA payments, via SEPA Credit Transfer through TARGET2 or EBA Clearing STEP2. For documentary-trade corridors, an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Luxembourg bank under UCP 600 is the preferred instrument for larger MLCC and resistor purchase contracts; sight-draft negotiation or deferred-payment acceptance against presentation of transport documents and inspection certificates provides standard seller protection. USD-denominated disbursements to Asian suppliers are routed through the bank's US correspondent using Fedwire or CHIPS settlement with an MT103 cover; pre-shipment and post-shipment working capital may be supported by documentary collection, import LC discounting, or receivables purchase agreements. All outbound payments undergo EU, UN, and OFAC sanctions screening on the beneficiary, the intermediary bank, and the destination country; the CSSF imposes no independent currency-export verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD FX swaps (overnight indexed and rolling spot)
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps on EUR/USD basis
European-style EUR/USD option contracts (call and put)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted non-convertible currencies such as CNY or INR, subject to the bank's EMIR margin framework, ISDA/CSA documentation, and internal credit-risk appetite

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Comptes annuels) filing and publication at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholder approval, and no later than 7 months after financial year-end (i.e., for a 31 Dec year-end: submit by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial injunction to file, fines of EUR 500 to 5,000 against legal representatives, and public strike-off initiated after 2 warnings from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Owner (UBO) Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), administered by the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following the anniversary date of the company's RCS registration; additionally within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 1,250, or EUR 125,000 for serious directors appointed in proof cases; repeated violation may trigger administrative strike-off for non-trading entities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined Annual Corporate Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax, Municipal Business Tax, Net Wealth Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the following tax year; extension normally granted to 31 December upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest on late payment at 0.8% per month; administrative fines from EUR 250 up to EUR 25,000; criminal prosecution for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Mandatory Review/Update of the Statutory Registers and Share Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Office – statutory registers physically available for inspection by the RCS and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous; must reflect any changes to shareholders, directors, or share pledges by the date of the Annual General Meeting (within 6 months of year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 2,500 for administrative non-compliance; loss of claim to limited liability for unfulfilled register maintenance obligations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the three Luxembourg size thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average headcount above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, as amended) for the annual accounts; consolidated accounts may use IFRS in accordance with EU Regulation 1606/2002.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must register all individuals having ultimate ownership or control (25% or more of shares or voting rights) with the RBE. The UBO declaration must be confirmed annually within 30 days after the anniversary of the RCS registration. Upon any shareholding transfer, a new declaration must be filed within 30 days, including the nationality, birth date, nature/extent of interest, and supporting documentation of the new UBO.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Pledges
Register of References to Bearer Securities (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (not required below thresholds); USD 7,000 – 20,000 if threshold-exceeding audit becomes mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (maximum aggregate CIT rate in Luxembourg City: 17% corporate income tax plus 7% unemployment fund surcharge plus 6.75% municipal business tax on taxable income, with the effective combined rate varying by commune; the 24.94% headline rate assumes Luxembourg City and includes the solidarity surcharge)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains under Sec. 166 LIR; 80% exemption on notional interest deduction for net equity increases under Sec. 168bis LIR; 30% patent box exemption on net IP income derived from qualifying IP under Sec. 50bis LIR; Luxembourg Innovation Act (R&D tax credit of base 20% on eligible R&D costs with enhanced rate for collaboration with research institutes); special purpose vehicles and intermediate holding companies may reduce effective tax via participation exemption and foreign tax credit mechanisms.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return (Formulaire 510 CIT/IRC), municipal business tax return (Formulaire 510 NBC), net wealth tax return (Formulaire 540) filed electronically via MyGuichet / eTVA platform of the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard filing deadline is 31 December for tax years aligned with the calendar year, extended to 30 June of the following year for tax representatives or with approved extension; in practice the ACD grants filing by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; six-month extension to 30 June if filed through a certified tax advisor and with advance request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1a - Identification and administrative data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registered office, Luxembourg RCS registration number (B number), tax file number (matricule), fiscal year start and end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL must provide Luxembourg permanent establishment nexus and branch registration details; confirm PE treaty attribution under Luxembourg DTA network.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 1b - Legal form and corporate data
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of legal form (Société à Responsabilité Limitée - SARL), date of incorporation, share capital structure, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporate shareholders, include direct and indirect ownership percentages to substantiate treaty eligibility and participation exemption analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 101-130 - Commercial and accounting profit computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net income (résultat comptable) per Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS if applied, adjusted to taxable result; reconcile book-to-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a detailed reconciliation of the Luxembourg financial statements to the taxable base; non-resident with Luxembourg PE must allocate income and costs to the PE under OECD-consistent attributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption claimed on dividends and capital gains, IP box deduction, notional interest deduction, charitable deductions, and other non-deductible expenses added back (e.g. hidden profit distributions, excessive interest, 50% of director fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide evidence of DTA treaty residence certificate (form 720) and underlying substantial shareholding conditions (minimum 10% participation, 12-month holding period, taxed-subject requirement) to claim the Luxembourg participation exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 191-220 - Taxable income and net wealth calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, municipal business tax base (deductible 75% of net worth interest expenses for CCT calculation), and net wealth tax return cross-references.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax only if PE or real estate in Luxembourg; complete Form 540 with PE net book assets and deductible carryforwards.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex - Transfer pricing disclosure (Form 720 / TP documentation notification)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annex disclosing controlled transactions, intangible property held, group financing, and cross-border related party flows; used by ACD for TP risk assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Passive electronic component distribution SARL must disclose intercompany purchase of multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors, inventory holding arrangements, and commission or resale margin models.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule for treaty withholding tax relief on outbound interest, royalty, or dividend payments; required foreign tax credit computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit the approved Luxembourg withholding tax refund or exemption application if treaty rate reduction applicable; TRC of the non-resident parent and certificate of fiscality are mandatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic increase of 0.6% per month on assessed tax up to a maximum of 10% of the tax amount; if no tax is due, a fixed fine up to EUR 1,000 may be imposed; failure to submit required annexes may trigger a penalty of EUR 250 per missing annex; deliberate failure or omission can lead to criminal fine (amende) of EUR 1,500 to EUR 750,000 and imprisonment in severe tax evasion cases; interest for late payment (intérêt de retard) accrues at 0.6% per month from the statutory due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on Luxembourg-source dividends paid on shares held by non-resident corporate shareholders, subject to the parent-subsidiary directive transposition and DTA reductions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduction on outbound dividends, the recipient must be the beneficial owner, hold shares for at least 12 months where the treaty requires it, and obtain a Luxembourg Form 720 residence certificate issued by the Luxembourg ACD; the paying SARL then applies the reduced rate at source or, if the full 15% was withheld, the non-resident shareholder must file a Luxembourg withholding tax refund claim (Form 718) within 5 years; an advance tax ruling from the Luxembourg Inland Revenue is recommended to fast-track treaty application, and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive route requires 10% shareholding and avoids WHT entirely in qualifying EU chains subject to anti-abuse measures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20% withholding tax reduced to 0% for EU/EEA-related payments under the Interest and Royalties Directive, otherwise treaty rates typically 0-10% (e.g. 0% under several OECD DTAs); interest: statutory withholding tax of 20% generally, but Luxembourg does not levy WHT on interest paid to non-resident companies in many treaty situations; under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, qualifying related-company payments bear 0% WHT; domestic anti-abuse rules require substance and beneficial ownership to retain treaty and directive relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,500,000 for transactions with related parties in Luxembourg (OECD TP documentation, including Master File and Local File) where the turnover threshold exceeds EUR 3,000,000; Luxembourg law requires a contemporaneous TP documentation file to be maintained if the group’s consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000 and intra-group transaction thresholds exceed EUR 1,500,000 (financial) or EUR 300,000 (non-financial) per year; the ACD circular LIR 56/1 - 56/2 prescribes the content of the Master File and Local File.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies a substance-over-form doctrine under Allgemeines Steuerrecht and OECD standards; since the 2019 Finance Law and EU ATAD, the ACD can disregard a Luxembourg entity lacking minimum economic substance (board meetings in Luxembourg, local strategic decisions, employees, office premises, operational risk, bank accounts) and re-characterise it as a shell; the EU DAC6 and ATAD1/ATAD2 contain a general anti-abuse rule (GAAR) that denies treaty benefits where a transaction lacks commercial rationale; the Luxembourg relationship (Section 166bis LIR) denies participation exemption to vehicles without taxable substance or where the income is not subject to adequate taxation in the source state.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of inventory revenue, artificial under-pricing of imported passive electronic components, fabrication of resale margins, or use of an offshore conduit to shift profits out of Luxembourg without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax reassessment up to 200% of the evaded tax (Luxembourg GAAR, abuse of law doctrine); criminal fine under Loi fiscale of EUR 1,500 to EUR 150,000 (increased where systematic); administrative surcharges of 10% plus 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; stripping of treaty benefits and denial of participation exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face personal civil liability for payment of taxes owed if they co-signed or knowingly received assets of the company in fraud of tax; travel bans may be imposed during criminal tax proceedings; imprisonment of 5 - 10 years in cases of aggravated tax fraud, with cumulative damages and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and retain the Luxembourg TP file (Master File/Local File) for controlled transactions with the trading parent or Asian manufacturing affiliate within the statutory filing deadline, or providing materially incomplete documentation; where turnover thresholds exceeded EUR 50M group and EUR 1.5M intra-group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Formal tax assessment based on deemed taxable margins estimated by the ACD; administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 for non-compliance with TP documentation obligations; penalty interest 5% per annum applied to adjustments; potential 10% late-filing penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director (gérant) of an SARL may be jointly liable with the company for TP documentation penalties if the director failed to exercise ordinary prudence; directors are exposed to criminal liability in a civil fraud suit by tax authorities seeking to pierce the veil where assets were dissipated intentionally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company absence of substance (economic substance doctrine violation)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Luxembourg SARL carrying only a registered office and mailbox functions, no local employees, no board meetings on Luxembourg soil, and all decisions taken by a foreign sole shareholder on behalf of a private equity fund, while claiming the benefits of the tax ruling or the participating exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg participation exemption; retroactive requalification of income as profit distribution subject to withholding tax; refusal of a Luxembourg tax residence certificate (Form 720) or withdrawal if already issued; anti-abuse directive on shell entities (EU ATAD/shell proposal framework) requiring reclassification of the tax residence to the jurisdiction of the parent, losses and penalties assessed accordingly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the additional tax claimed if they certified the substance declarations in tax returns; under Luxembourg law, directors can be held liable for the company’s tax debts in cases of manifest serious negligence; imprisonment possible if participation in a criminal shell-company arrangement is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and criminal enforcement (money laundering of tax proceeds)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funnelling under-invoiced passive electronic inventory sales through a Luxembourg bank account or through a third-party payment rail into a holding account, while the invoices disguise the true ultimate beneficial owner; exceeding EUR 10,000 of criminal proceeds derived from foreign tax evasion triggers Luxembourg AML obligations under CSSF Circular 17/650.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Forfeiture of funds equal to the laundered values; fine of up to EUR 10,000,000 for legal entities under Article 506-2 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code; statutory mandates under the fiscal criminal law apply; exclusion from public procurement and potential order of dissolution of the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly participating in laundering face imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and a fine of up to EUR 50,000 under the Criminal Code; AML compliance officers and managing directors are subject to CSSF sanctions including personal fines up to EUR 500,000 and suspension; civil reparation and worldwide asset-tracing orders follow.
